# The Trade Method

> A learning notebook of day trading setups, written down before the open. Each setup page gives the thesis, the stages, the filters, the entry, the stop and backtest results (losing results included), with an annotated chart walkthrough and a TradingView Pine Script where one exists. Fundamentals pages cover the process behind every setup: edge, price action, support and resistance mistakes, relative volume, trailing stops, exits, the six momentum trades, order flow for beginners, how to get better at trading faster and the options expected move.

Educational content only, not financial advice. Times are US Eastern; examples use US stocks and ETFs on intraday charts.

## Setups

- [All setups](https://thetrademethod.com/setups/): every setup on one page, filterable by session (opening drive, all session, swing) and side.
- [PMH Break — the opening drive, run mechanically](https://thetrademethod.com/setups/pmh-break.html): Price reclaims the premarket high on the opening drive and holds it. The break is the entry; the reclaim level is the invalidation.
- [Market Memory — the day two model, run mechanically](https://thetrademethod.com/setups/market-memory.html): Yesterday's real buyers and sellers left a map. Price returns to those levels and reacts on the John Wick candle, the confirmed rejection that says which way memory is pulling it.
- [Fashionably Late — scalp the cross, not the bottom](https://thetrademethod.com/setups/fashionably-late.html): Let the low print, let momentum build back to VWAP, and buy the moment the 9 EMA crosses it — proof the turn already happened, not a guess that it will.
- [Energy in the Tank — the volatility cycle breakout](https://thetrademethod.com/setups/energy-in-the-tank.html): A squeeze on the higher time frame stores energy. An outlier volume bar on the breakout is what spends it — the same signal behind some of the biggest continuation moves in recent memory.
- [Opening Range Break — the same range, every single day](https://thetrademethod.com/setups/opening-range-break.html): Let the first 15–30 minutes set the range, then trust the break only when volume and the higher time frame agree — the ticker changes, the mechanics never do.
- [Day Three Breakout — catalyst, inside day, and the break](https://thetrademethod.com/setups/day-three-breakout.html): A real catalyst drives day one, a quiet low-volume day sets up day two, and the break of that day-two high on day three is the entry — the same three-day sequence, six different tickers.
- [9 EMA Continuation — read the reclaim, not the touch](https://thetrademethod.com/setups/nine-ema-continuation.html): Don't chase the breakout — wait for the pullback into the 9 EMA, read whether buyers actually step back up, and enter on the reclaim, not the tap. Pine indicator included (/pine/nine-ema-continuation.pine).
- [MACD Scalping Strategy: 3/9/5 Continuation Scalp](https://thetrademethod.com/setups/macd-continuation-scalp.html): Let a flat consolidation build, wait for the expansion move, then trade the pullback — enter when the MACD line crosses back over the signal line on its side of zero, custom 3/9/5 settings, no histogram, stop under the dip, exit on the cross back. Pine indicator included. Our test of the video's rules on 5 years of 1-minute bars (12 large caps): 47,524 trades, -0.18R each, the same as random entries (-0.17R).
- [VWAP Reversal — three signals, one trade](https://thetrademethod.com/setups/vwap-reversal.html): Stack a VWAP band touch, an old horizontal level, and a failure-test reversal candle at the same price — one signal is a guess, three is a trade.
- [ATR Hybrid Scalp — band-touch longs, wick-reversal shorts](https://thetrademethod.com/setups/atr-band-hybrid.html): Longs and shorts run two completely different playbooks on the same chart — longs enter on a touch of a 3.1× ATR band and exit on a fixed 2/1. Pine indicator included (/pine/atr-band-hybrid.pine).
- [Cup and Handle — plan the trade, trade the plan](https://thetrademethod.com/setups/cup-and-handle.html): Five questions qualify the pattern — uptrend, a volume-confirmed cup, a tightening handle, clean air above, and sector/market alignment — then enter only on the break, sized off a 1.
- [Three-Candle CRT — sweep, confirm, break](https://thetrademethod.com/setups/three-candle-crt.html): Candle Range Theory in three candles — mark the extreme, wait for the sweep-and-close-back-in, then trade only the break — sized to an exact 1.
- [Volume Profile Trading System — PC, value area, breakout](https://thetrademethod.com/setups/volume-profile-system.html): One tool, read three different ways depending on how the prior session closed — a point-of-control bounce, a value-area reversal, or a value-area breakout continuation — all sized to a fixed 2R.
- [Volume S/R Rejection — volume-backed levels, confirmed on the close](https://thetrademethod.com/setups/volume-sr-rejection.html): Trade only the support and resistance the volume profile backs, mark where the point of control stacks on a level, and take the rejection when the bar closes and the volume balance flips your way.
- [GEX Levels — call wall, put wall, gamma flip](https://thetrademethod.com/setups/gex-levels.html): Dealer hedging leaves fingerprints at a few prices every morning. The walls say where price is likely to stall; the gamma flip says whether to fade them or follow the break.
- [Zero Lag Pullback — trade the reclaim, not the cross](https://thetrademethod.com/setups/zero-lag-pullback.html): Two zero-lag EMAs, 50 and 100, mark the trend. Wait for a close between them, then buy the green candle that closes back over the fast line on above-average volume. Stop on the slow line, target 2R.
- [Knock Twice — break, knock, break again](https://thetrademethod.com/setups/knock-twice.html): Price closes through an old swing high, runs, stays away for five bars, then comes back and knocks on the old level once and holds. Buy the knock with the stop a tick under it. The break of the new high confirms it, and T2 is one more leg.
- [Silver Bullet — ICT's magic hours, tested](https://thetrademethod.com/setups/silver-bullet.html): ICT's Silver Bullet as exact rules: in three one-hour New York windows, wait for a sweep of untouched liquidity, a displacement candle that leaves a fair value gap, and a limit at the gap's edge. Tested over 16 years on four futures markets, it lost money after costs in every hour.
- [Gap Give and Go: Opening Gap Trading Strategy](https://thetrademethod.com/setups/gap-give-and-go.html): The Gap Give and Go, from SMB Capital's playbook: a stock gaps on a real catalyst, gives back fast on light volume into a key level, holds in a neutral range, then goes. Buy the turn on the tape with the stop under the low of day, and target the open, the premarket high and half the RVOL times the ATR. Free TradingView indicator. Tested with the video's rules on 2,595 trades (Dec 2021 to Nov 2026): +0.06R a trade, against -0.18R for random entries on the same days.
- [Qullamaggie Breakout — buy the leaders, trail the 10-day](https://thetrademethod.com/setups/qullamaggie.html): Kristjan Kullamägi's (Qullamaggie) swing trading setup: find the top 1–2% momentum stocks, wait for a tight base on the 10 and 20-day averages, buy the opening range high on breakout day with the stop at the low of the day, sell a third after 3 to 5 days and trail the rest on the 10 or 20-day. Plus episodic pivots and parabolic shorts.
- [QQE Mod + EMA 50 — trade the color change with the trend](https://thetrademethod.com/setups/qqe-mod.html): QQE Mod plus the EMA 50 on a 5-minute gold chart: above the EMA, buy when the histogram turns from red to blue on a strong candle; below it, sell the mirror image. Enter at the next open, stop beyond the last swing, and take a 2R target only if the next level leaves room. With the Pine Script code.
- [Technical Catalyst Breakout — when the level is the news](https://thetrademethod.com/setups/technical-catalyst-breakout.html): SMB Capital's 8-step breakout blueprint for when there's no headline: a stock or ETF clears a 9 out of 10 higher-timeframe level it couldn't break for weeks (ETHA under 19.12 for over a month), on elevated RVOL and a volume spike on the breakout bar, with the tape paying the offer. Size to the market (A or B size), stop a penny past the round number under the breakout candle, add over consolidation pauses, exit on a defined signal, and scratch when the velocity isn't there.
- [Anchored VWAP Strategy for Earnings Swing Trades](https://thetrademethod.com/setups/anchored-vwap.html): SMB Capital's anchored VWAP method for earnings and catalyst swing trades: anchor the VWAP on the earnings release candle (or the bar where a catalyst like an election started the move) with the source set to the low, want at least 20% of the average daily volume after hours (50 to 70% is better), buy the day-one or day-two dip and reclaim at the open near the line, stop under it, and trail it on the daily chart: a daily close below the anchored VWAP means cut at least half. Pine indicator included (/pine/anchored-vwap.pine). Tested: loses, -0.18R over 22,554 earnings trades on 2,055 US stocks (2021-2026); the same rules on random anchors lost -0.77R.
- [The Strat — read the evidence, not the pattern](https://thetrademethod.com/setups/the-strat.html): The Strat (Rob Smith's method), from a video on reading smart money: price can only do three things from one bar to the next (stay inside, a 1; take out one side, a 2 up or 2 down; take out both, a 3), every 3 is a broadening formation whose other side is the target, time frame continuity (last price above or below the quarter, month, week and day opens) shows which group is more aggressive, and a simultaneous break (a sector and its holdings, or the indexes, breaking last week's level at the same time) is the evidence that institutional algorithms turned on. Enter as the break goes in force, stop just past the current bar, tighten on lower time frame inside bars, and hold winners. With the video's three Sunday-night calls: the energies, the bitcoin miners (WGMI) and the semis.
- [Hitchhiker Scalp Strategy: 9 EMA Pullback, Tested](https://thetrademethod.com/setups/hitchhiker-scalp.html): An SMB Capital trader's adapted version of SMB's hitchhiker scalp: instead of chasing a stock in play (abnormal volume, a large range and a reason) after an outsized move, wait for the first pullback toward the 9 EMA on the 2-minute chart, on lighter volume than the move, and enter as it slows and the trend resumes. The initial stop is a 2-minute close past the 21 EMA (size from it), tightened to the most recent high or low once it works; take about 70% off into momentum in small pieces (about 5% at a time) and trail the last 30% on the prior 2-minute bar. Skip chop, stocks not in play, late (third, fourth, fifth) pullbacks and heavy opposing volume. With the video's SOXL short (breakdown level 98.80) and long (98 to nearly 103, pullback near 101). Free TradingView indicator. Tested on 16,136 trades (2-minute, SPY, QQQ and 10 large caps, Nov 2021 to Nov 2026): break-even, +0.006R a trade.
- [Liquidity Refill Strategy: the Two-Candle Imbalance](https://thetrademethod.com/setups/liquidity-refill.html): A quant's two-candle pattern built on order book microstructure (aggression against liquidity refill): after a relatively big candle (C1) out of compression, the next candle (C2) makes a quick early wick (first 10–15 seconds on a 1-minute chart) that stays in C1's top 10–20% and gets absorbed; enter when C2 crosses C1's high (low for shorts), stop just past the wick, exit after three or four candles, on the first opposite candle or at an obvious level like the previous day's low; one retest of C2's open on a lower time frame as a second chance; skip chop, late wicks, deep wicks and C3 breaks. Any time frame, long or short. Tested with the video's rules on a year of NQ futures, wick timed to the second from real trades: no edge (1-minute: 193 trades, -0.36R a trade, worse than random entries).
- [Look Above and Fail Strategy: the Value Area Fade](https://thetrademethod.com/setups/look-above-and-fail.html): A prop trader's balance-day model on NQ and ES 2-minute charts: let the developing regular-hours volume profile build for 30 minutes, trade only at the value area high and low, and when aggressive orders push past an edge and price comes right back inside, trade the reclaim (market order on a fast flip, or the retest that holds), stop past the big trades, partial at POC, target the other side of value; skip trending days, news and a range that has stopped you three times. Pine indicator included. Our test of the video's rules on a year of NQ trades: 874 trades, -0.33R each, worse than random entries (-0.15R).
- [Micro Range — the range after the range, a regime-first breakout filter](https://thetrademethod.com/setups/micro-range.html): Institutional trader Imre Gams (Chart Fanatics) on trading balance and imbalance: map the regime with strict one time framing (higher high, higher low and higher close) on the weekly and daily, read the macro through the Fed's inflation and employment mandate, mark value zones from weekly, cash-session and overnight profiles, never buy the first breakout (price, not value), wait for the micro range (the range after the range), then buy the absorbed flush back into it (plan A) or aggressive buying out of it (plan B) with one risk budget split between them; in balance, the failed auction at the value edges in two flavors (V-shape reversal and slow burn).
- [Fibonacci OTE — buy the pullback at 0.702, the optimal trade entry](https://thetrademethod.com/setups/fib-ote.html): Com Lucro Trader on the Fibonacci retracement and ICT's Optimal Trade Entry as one entry model: price moves in impulses and pullbacks, draw the fib on the latest impulse (1 on the swing, 0 on the end), pullbacks under 0.382 are noise, 0.382–0.5 is a poor reward to risk, 0.5–0.618 is the Golden Zone, buy in discount and sell in premium, then a limit at 0.702 inside the 0.618–0.786 OTE (ICT's original is 0.62/0.705/0.79), stop past the swing, half off just short of the old high with the stop to break even, the rest at the next higher time frame level, only with room to that level. Strategy two: a major support/resistance level, a double bottom or top one time frame down, the neckline break, then a limit at 0.618 of the break. Walkthrough on made-up gold bars, a depth slider, a trade calculator, and a Pine v6 TradingView indicator for strategy one (/pine/fib-ote.pine).
- [The 10 AM ORB — an opening range breakout that waits for 10:00](https://thetrademethod.com/setups/ten-am-orb.html): Peachy Investor's opening range breakout for ES and NQ futures, as traded by her New York session coach Goose: set a larger point of view bias before the open and skip level 3 news and FOMC days; no trades from 9:30 to 9:45 ET, when fakeouts are most common; mark the 15-minute range high, low and 50% at 9:45 and the 30-minute range at 10:00; the first break with the bias is confirmation, not the entry; enter around 10:00 on a retest of the range edge or a higher low (lower high for shorts), stop past the reaction, target the next key level at 1:2 or better; break-even once it works, base hits inside a wide range, the 50% rule on a big range, and a shakeout into the 11:00 hourly candle
- [Gamma Wall Footprint — three GEX setups confirmed by the footprint](https://thetrademethod.com/setups/gamma-wall-footprint.html): Skydweller.trades' three NQ futures setups at the gamma levels: mark the put wall, the call wall and zero gamma from the GEX map before the open; above zero gamma dealer hedging absorbs moves (the lake), below it hedging adds fuel (the rapids); a slow approach to a wall means look for the reaction right at it, a fast approach means let it overshoot and enter on the reclaim; confirm on the footprint with absorption, stacked imbalances (three or more rows at 3 to 1), a delta flip or trapped traders. Stop where the wall idea is proven wrong (often 30 to 50 ticks on NQ), half off at the first reaction, the rest to the next level; entering close is about 8.5R, chasing late is 0.5R. Examples: long 25,156 off a 25,150 put wall to zero gamma (+94), short 25,447 under a 25,450 call wall after an overshoot (+127). The third play goes with the break when price loses zero gamma and holds. Skip single flow prints, broken walls, OPEX/triple witching/VIX expiration, and trades after a loss that are off plan.
- [Heatmap Scalp: Order Flow Scalping with VWAP](https://thetrademethod.com/setups/heatmap-scalp.html): Funded trader Matthias's order flow scalp on NQ and ES futures from an IQ Capital live session: market structure and the session VWAP set the side, a liquidity heatmap (Bookmap) times the pullback entry on the bid, a fixed dollar stop, adds on pullbacks, exit before the wall. Tested on a year of NQ with real order flow: 163 trades, 29% win, -0.01R a trade vs random -0.04R, break-even, no clear edge; the heatmap's resting orders are untested. Free TradingView indicator.
- [Ready, Aim, Fire — trend, level, then an order flow trigger](https://thetrademethod.com/setups/ready-aim-fire.html): Zach Boyjian's three-step NQ/ES order flow strategy from an IQ Capital interview: ready (the higher time frame regime from daily structure, trend or balance, plus the news calendar), aim (static levels marked before the open: yesterday's full session value area high, POC and value area low, the prior day high and low, the overnight high and low, session VWAP, composite high volume nodes and GEX walls; wait for price to reach one, ideally stacked), fire (on 5-minute volume profile candles with big trades: one side puts in effort without reward at the level, then a rejection; market order on the break back through or after the close). Stop past the defended high or low with room (about 50 ticks on NQ to start), target the next area of interest at 1:1 or better or skip it, then hands off. Walkthrough on made-up 5-minute NQ bars, a trade checker, a winner and a loser, and a planner.
- [ICT Made Simple: ICT Trading Strategy Explained](https://thetrademethod.com/setups/ict-made-simple.html): Trader Mayne's ICT framework stripped to six pieces: trend (clear and obvious higher highs and higher lows or lower highs and lower lows, else sideways; three candle swings), structure (a candle body closing through the last swing is a market structure break, breaking the last higher low a market structure shift), the range (significant low to high of the current leg with a fib at 0, 0.5 and 1: premium above, discount below, the 0.618–0.786 OTE with the 0.705 sweet spot), three points of interest (order blocks, breakers, fair value gaps; the one in the discount wins ties), and external vs internal range liquidity (the draw is the opposite of what was just taken). Then the two time frame rule: map on the high time frame, and when price reaches the POI drop to the low time frame (weekly to daily, daily to 1-hour, 4-hour to 15-minute, 1-hour to 5-minute) and enter on the breaker after a low is taken and the high that took it breaks; stop under the turn, target external range liquidity. Walkthrough on made-up weekly and daily BTC bars, a trade checker, three low time frame scripts and a planner. Tested: the video's rules (which take both of its Bitcoin trades) made +2.45R a trade on Bitcoin, but on only 28 trades since 2016; across every liquid US stock they lost -0.05R a trade over 26,629 trades, and every intraday pairing lost.

## Trading basics

- [Trading basics](https://thetrademethod.com/basics/): start here if you're new. Plain-English pages grouped into four topics: markets and instruments (how futures work, how options work, investment funds, EPS and the P/E ratio, 24-hour stock trading, covered calls), orders and execution (order flow for beginners, arbitrage), reading charts (fundamental vs technical vs macro analysis, relative volume, six momentum trades), and risk and money (where your stop belongs, dynamic risk sizing, investing through a recession).

## Trading fundamentals

- [All fundamentals](https://thetrademethod.com/fundamentals/): every fundamentals page on one page, filterable by type (framework, self-check, process, options).
- [Inch Wide, Mile Deep — the process behind every setup](https://thetrademethod.com/edge.html): Where trading edge actually comes from: reading the tape, scoping a catalyst and setup, and starting with your stop. Inch wide, mile deep.
- [Support & Resistance Mistakes — the five that cost the most](https://thetrademethod.com/mistakes.html): The five support and resistance mistakes that cost traders the most, and how to correct each one. The level is just an input; the mistakes are the cost.
- [Three Price Action Rules — continuation, stops, and adding right](https://thetrademethod.com/price-action-rules.html): Three price action rules used across every trade: the continuation pattern, defining your stop before entry, and adding to a winner the right way.
- [Trailing Stop Exits — four styles, one system](https://thetrademethod.com/trailing-stops.html): Four trailing stop styles for exiting a trade you already have edge on, protecting it from selling too early and from overstaying too long.
- [Let Winners Run — exits that grow your average winner](https://thetrademethod.com/let-winners-run.html): Three exit rules that let a winning trade keep paying. Same entries, same stops: let the move, not a fixed target, decide when you get out.
- [Relative Volume — is anyone actually showing up?](https://thetrademethod.com/relative-volume.html): Relative volume (RVOL) and the cumulative RVOL histogram: is a stock doing abnormal volume compared to itself, and is that participation increasing, holding, fading or absent?
- [Six Momentum Trades — the mechanisms under every strategy name](https://thetrademethod.com/six-momentum-trades.html): The six momentum trades underneath almost every strategy name: breakout, breakout and retest, pullback continuation, consolidation continuation, trend continuation and reclaim, plus the checklist that comes before entry.
- [Four Pillars — levels, context, sizing, discipline](https://thetrademethod.com/four-pillars.html): A simple, repeatable trading framework in four pillars: the levels price keeps reacting to, the context around them, position sizing that keeps you in the game, and the discipline to follow your plan.
- [Get Better Faster — compress the learning cycle](https://thetrademethod.com/get-better-faster.html): How to get better at trading faster: narrow to one repeatable setup, build a real playbook, compress your reps with replay and review, risk small enough to learn, find the see-it moment, review like film, and run the learning cycle.
- [Dynamic Risk Sizing — press the A, coast the C](https://thetrademethod.com/dynamic-risk-sizing.html): Why static sizing drains your P&L: two traders take the same three trades (an A premarket high break, a B+ second chance short, and a B− range break followed by an A big dog consolidation break), one risks $200 every time, the other sizes each trade to its grade. The A+, A, B, C risk tiering model, the variables that move a grade, and how to build your tiers from 20 examples of each trade.
- [Order Flow for Beginners — read four things, at one level](https://thetrademethod.com/order-flow.html): Order flow trading for beginners, from a Trader Dale video and book: what a footprint chart shows (contracts traded at the bid and ask at every price), who shows up on each side, the platform and level 1 futures data you need, the four things to read (large orders or high volume nodes, volume clusters, delta, stacked imbalances), using order flow as confirmation at a volume profile point of control, the absorption setup, four confirmations (big limit orders, absorption, aggressive orders and delta, cumulative delta divergence), the level-finding setups, trade management and a beginner action plan.
- [Linda Raschke's Trading Rules — get the main idea right](https://thetrademethod.com/linda-raschke.html): Lessons from a long interview with Market Wizard Linda Raschke: read price instead of order flow (one watch, not two), the volume spike test (drop to the 1-minute chart and about 80% of spikes land on a prior intraday swing high or low, where algorithms trigger), get the main idea of the day right (low-to-high or high-to-low day, the first hour's range, the two-day rhythm), choose exits in ATR (half-ATR target, three-ATR target, a 2.5-ATR volatility trailing stop, time stop; a trail is the best exit only about 15% of the time), all in, all out instead of scaling, one even bet size from the average daily dollar range reset every quarter, cut size in a discretionary drawdown but hold it in a system, her four profit centers and routine.
- [How to Trade Earnings — headline, call, then price](https://thetrademethod.com/trading-earnings.html): A four-step process for trading earnings from an SMB Capital video: watch the headline reaction without chasing it (SpaceX spiked above 150 toward 152 on the beat and faded back within minutes), listen to the conference call for contracts, next-quarter guidance, financing, dilution and share unlocks, wait for price to confirm at a level (the long came around 154 after the call, with follow-through through 156), then build Plan A (hold 155–156, a possible close above 160) and Plan B (lose it as about $500 billion of spending to finance and about 900 million unlocking shares add supply). Includes a Tesla-style contrast where the call reverses a good first reaction.
- [Seven Trading Traps — why experienced traders lose money](https://thetrademethod.com/seven-trading-traps.html): The seven traps that make experienced traders lose money, from SMB Capital's desk reset meeting (Mike Bellafiore): the "not my market" excuse, style drift (trading outside your proven playbook and time frame), missing a regime change (a three-part QQQ filter: near the all-time high, above the 20-day and 50-day moving averages, else defensive scalping), holding out for grand slams (hard give-back rules), not selective enough (downgrade a setup three notches when one nuance is missing in a tough tape; fold when the flop doesn't fit), too few short-term "easy money" trades (turn trades, tape scalps, low floats, breaking news), sizing poorly (size up when a setup is hot, cut 50% or more in a drawdown, never desperation size) and overusing options (if you wouldn't hold the stock through the level, don't hold the option), plus the five-point reset checklist.
- [Auction Market Theory — where to start from zero](https://thetrademethod.com/auction-market-theory.html): Auction market theory from a Fabio Valentini video on what he would study first if he started trading from zero: identify the market regime before anything else (balance, transition, imbalance; the market as an elastic band of extension and snapback, with fundamental catalysts ending balance), trade wall to wall inside balance with initiative auction candles and absorption at 1:1.5 to 1:2 rather than 1:5, the transition candle where big orders accept value outside the area, the asymmetrical opportunity when a low volume node leads to a far-away next value, a profile of the move from A to B with the delta peak and value area low plus a margin of error for the stop, position building by moving the stop to the last invalidation and risking one third of the locked profit (worst case still green), reading each session's auction (accepted lower, failed auction tails, accepted above, fading the value area low) and intraday candle framing with the change of flow (POC migration). Six animated walkthroughs on made-up bars.
- [Thesis to Trade — levels, price action, patience](https://thetrademethod.com/thesis-to-trade.html): Vincent Desiano's full daily trading system from a live stream: build levels only on the weekly, daily, 4-hour and hourly charts and group the lowest low with the nearby lows into one zone (about 20-30 points on the S&P future, about 100 on the Nasdaq), skip levels above a clearly rejecting high, run the same morning routine across futures, ETFs and sectors, think through each level with market structure and a written game plan (fade a failure at 7,600, otherwise no trade), only watch price action inside the zones, expect traps and sweeps at the level (the sweep and reclaim), enter on the break and retest (retest and reject, or reclaim and hold) only after confirmation instead of front-running the idea, don't short into a 200 moving average or the previous day low but short the previous day low break and retest, watch the first one-minute candle low as an experiment, and manage trending trades with intraday structure and the EMA cloud. Levels, price action, self-control. Five animated walkthroughs on made-up bars plus a five-step stepper.
- [Pyramiding Into Winners — add smaller, risk less](https://thetrademethod.com/pyramiding.html): SMB Capital on adding to a winning trade: pyramiding vs martingale, the first entry at 1R and every add smaller (0.5R, 0.25R, down to 0.1R) with the stop moved in your favor each time, a fashionably late model where a 0.5R add near a 3R target leaves the worst case at +2.5R, AMD and CBRS opening range break examples, why an add on volume alone is not pyramiding, and two questions before every add.
- [Stacked Imbalances — order flow levels with a small stop](https://thetrademethod.com/stacked-imbalances.html): Two videos on stacked imbalances. Orderflows: an imbalance compares the bid at one price with the offer one tick higher (20 vs 150) at about 4 to 1, three or more in a row make a stack, markets have memory so price returns to it, the payroll long (stack 3,973–3,974, bid 3,974, stop 3,973, rally to 3,994), stacks that hold, go one tick through, go sideways or fail, and the 3,921–3,922 short. Futures Flow: horizontal imbalances at 400% on NQ, where the stack sits in the candle (mid-body vs wick), passive orders and trapped buyers or sellers, waiting for a large participant (the 128-lot buyer) before taking the reaction, and support flipping to resistance.
- [Level Radar — the odds price reaches a key level today](https://thetrademethod.com/level-radar.html): The Good, The Bad And The Bitcoin's free Level Radar indicator for TradingView and NinjaTrader: the previous day's high, low and close, the overnight high and low, the open, the opening range (first 30 minutes) and today's high and low, each with the chance in percent that price touches it before the session ends. How the odds are worked out (distance against the average range of the last ten sessions, shrunk by the square root of the time left and adjusted for today's pace, checked against 15 years of ES, NQ, YM and GC data and the last 20 sessions of your chart; a random-walk formula on crypto and forex), session settings, the ranking panel and scoreboard, and three uses: realistic targets, a filter for low-odds setups, and timing as the odds fall. Includes the full Pine Script source.
- [Seven Cheat Codes — the simple rules of a profitable scalper](https://thetrademethod.com/seven-cheat-codes.html): Scarface Trades' seven rules from his video "Trading is a Video Game, Here are the Cheat Codes": find a strategy with a proven edge (three scalping setups: the pre-market high and low from 4:00 to 9:30 a.m. Eastern with the entry on the retest instead of the break, the one candle rule where the last down-close candle supports an uptrend and the last up-close candles cap a downtrend, and the 5-minute opening range break and retest), master market structure (uptrend, downtrend, range; trade the trends, skip the range), combine time frames (daily for the direction, 1-minute for the entry, about $670 risked for about $2,070), most scalps should work within five minutes or you're out, start with small size and scale up slowly, trade only A+ conditions (a choppy day vs a trend day with the same setups), and practice every day. Five animated walkthroughs on made-up bars, a which-trade-is-higher-probability quiz, a position size calculator and a five-step stepper.
- [Eight Trading Rules — how to get profitable again after a slump](https://thetrademethod.com/eight-trading-rules.html): SMB Capital's video "These 8 Trading Rules Can Make You Profitable" with Mike Bellafiore, given to a firm trader in a slump: struggle is part of the process but not changing isn't; Shark's way out of a slump (when in doubt get out, take a personal inventory in a journal, trade smaller, book a green day); Dr. Brett Steenbarger on diagnosing slumps early; famous traders' advice; rule out a changed market first (2022 rate hikes); then the eight rules: lower your size and risk, be more selective (trades that fall into your lap), shorten your time frame, don't do this alone, one good trade, a daily report card on good entries, keep your heart rate low and measure it in real time, and write your solution down and send it to a mentor. Six animated walkthroughs on made-up data, a which-rules-fit-your-slump checker, an entry report card and a five-step stepper.
- [Where Your Stop Belongs — put your stop where the thesis dies](https://thetrademethod.com/stop-placement.html): SMB Capital's video "The Stop Technique that Will Take You to the Trading Big Leagues" with Jeff Holden: why the low of the day is often the wrong stop for a quick breakout, and the one question that should decide a stop (what would price have to do to prove this trade has changed?). An opening range break claims price leaves the range and stays out, so its stop goes where that claim dies (back in the range and under VWAP). The $50 hypothetical (target 50.60, session-low stop 49.40 is one to one at best); a real CoreWeave (CRWV) review: long about 57.82 on the pre-market high break, target 60, stop at the 54 low of day (risking about 3.82 to make 2.18) vs just under VWAP near 56 vs just under the range at 57, with the reward to risk and break-even win rate for each; starting wide and moving the stop up (am I wrong if it drops VWAP, the pre-market high, the opening price?); the same morning's turn trade at 54 with a stop just under the level (the best turn trades risk 10 to 20 cents to make a dollar); why a closer stop isn't free and should be checked against your own sample; writing the invalidation before entry; and Bill Ackman's 2022 Netflix exit as thesis discipline. Four animated walkthroughs on made-up bars, a reward-to-risk and break-even calculator, a pick-your-stop question, a wide vs closer stop expected-value calculator and a five-step stepper.
- [How Futures Work — contracts, margin and leverage for beginners](https://thetrademethod.com/futures-basics.html): Martik Finance's video "How Futures Trading Really Work (Full Beginner's Guide)": a futures contract is an agreement to buy or sell a set amount at a set price on a set date, an obligation for both sides (unlike an option, where the buyer can walk away). The farmer and bread company wheat deal (5,000 bushels at $6), hedgers and speculators, commodity, stock index, interest rate, currency and crypto futures, long and short, closing with the opposite trade, physical delivery vs cash settlement. Contract size and tick value (crude oil 1,000 barrels with a $10 tick, gold 100 troy ounces, the E-mini S&P 500 at $50 times the index with a $12.50 tick). Margin as a security deposit, not a loan: about $10,000 controls about $200,000 of gold, so a 5% move is a 100% swing on the deposit. Daily mark to market, initial and maintenance margin, margin calls and forced liquidation. Futures vs spot, the futures curve, contango and backwardation, and April 20, 2020, when the expiring May WTI crude contract settled at minus $37.63 because storage was full. The six risks: leverage, losses beyond the deposit, daily cash settlement, forced exits on margin calls, expiration, and thin contracts. Three animated walkthroughs on made-up prices, a contract-value and tick calculator, a leverage and margin-call calculator, and a five-step checklist before a first futures trade.
- [Investment Funds Explained — three questions for any fund](https://thetrademethod.com/investment-funds.html): Martik Finance's video "Every Investment Fund Explained in 12 Minutes (Beginner's Guide)": a fund pools money to buy many investments at once (diversification) and charges a yearly expense ratio. Three questions explain almost any fund: how you buy it (a mutual fund from the fund company at NAV once a day, an ETF on the exchange all day, a closed-end fund that can trade above or below its holdings, private hedge, private equity and venture funds for accredited investors, hedge funds traditionally 2% plus 20%), who decides what it buys (an index fund copies a list like the S&P 500 and is not a package; active managers mostly trail the S&P 500 in a typical year), and what's inside (money market, bond, dividend, sector and thematic, real estate and commodity funds), plus target-date funds and leveraged and inverse ETFs. $10,000 for 30 years at 7% before fees ends near $75,000 at 0.05% and near $57,000 at 1%; a +3%/−3% month leaves the index under 1% lower and a 3x fund almost 8% lower.
- [How Options Work — calls, puts, premium and break-even for beginners](https://thetrademethod.com/options-basics.html): Martik Finance's video "How Options Really Work (Full Beginner's Guide)": an option is the right, not the obligation, to buy (call) or sell (put) 100 shares at a strike price until expiration, for a premium (like a house deposit). Anna buys a $100 call for $200: at $120 she makes $1,800, at $100, $95 or $50 she loses only $200; Marco, the seller, keeps the $200 with open-ended risk. Puts, in, at and out of the money, break-even (strike plus premium, $102; put strike minus premium, $98), time decay that accelerates near expiration, the volatility crush ($200 to $80 after earnings), buying back a short option, selling the contract instead of exercising, hedging, covered calls, speculation, and American-style early assignment.
- [EPS and the P/E Ratio — earnings per share and what you pay for it](https://thetrademethod.com/eps-pe-ratio.html): Two Martik Finance videos on one page. EPS is net income minus preferred dividends, divided by shares outstanding (Company A: $4.80; Company B: $3.85 despite higher net income); EPS rises with profit and buybacks and falls with dilution; negative EPS isn't automatically a bad investment. The P/E ratio is price divided by EPS ($100 / $10 = 10, about 10 years of earnings), varies by industry (growth high, mature or cyclical low), is best compared with the industry average (FreshBite 10, Tasty Treats 15, average 12), and comes trailing (last 12 months, real) or forward (estimates; BrightTech 20 trailing, 10 forward, 25 if the estimate drops).
- [What Arbitrage Is — one asset, two prices](https://thetrademethod.com/arbitrage.html): Martik Finance's video "What is Arbitrage? How Traders Make Risk-Free Profits": buy where an asset is cheap and sell the same asset where it's expensive, at the same time ($100 and $105: $5 a unit before fees). Gaps come from different exchanges, regions and information lag. Spatial, triangular (currency loops) and merger or risk arbitrage. It's low risk but not risk free: execution, fees (0.2% a side against a 1 to 2% gap), liquidity and transfer delays. High-frequency firms with co-located servers, direct feeds, low fees and capital get almost all of it, and arbitrage itself closes the gap and keeps markets efficient.
- [Fundamental vs Technical vs Macro Analysis — three ways to read a market](https://thetrademethod.com/analysis-types.html): Martik Finance's video: fundamental analysis (what a company is worth: quantitative numbers from the income statement, balance sheet and cash flow, and qualitative brand, leadership, competitive advantage and industry trends; subjective, forecast-based, and vulnerable to hidden bad news like Enron), technical analysis (price, volume, uptrends and downtrends, support and resistance, breakouts and fakeouts; visual and quick, but shows what not why), and macro analysis (monetary policy and interest rates, fiscal policy, GDP, unemployment, consumer confidence, manufacturing, the economic calendar and geopolitics; good for index funds, silent on single companies).
- [Investing Through a Recession — what the data says](https://thetrademethod.com/recession-investing.html): Martik Finance's video "How to Invest During a Recession (What the Data Actually Says)": recessions are dangerous because of what investors do, not the drop itself. In the US the NBER calls recessions months late (the 2007–09 start announced Dec 1, 2008; 2020's on Jun 8, 2020). 34 recessions since the 1850s, about 10 to 11 months on average since World War II, 18 months in 2007–09, 2 months in 2020. Three mistakes: recency bias, waiting for good news (March 2020 had two of the ten worst and two of the eleven best S&P 500 days), and confusing the backward-looking economy with the forward-looking market. Decide contributions, extra contributions, the emergency fund and a rebalancing trigger in advance.
- [24-Hour Stock Trading — what changes on Sunday, Dec 6, 2026](https://thetrademethod.com/24-hour-stock-trading.html): Important information on the new near-24-hour US stock trading hours. From Sunday, Dec 6, 2026 at 9 PM ET, stocks trade from Sunday 9 PM to Friday 8 PM, with a one-hour pause from 8 to 9 PM each weeknight. A new overnight session runs 9 PM to 4 AM ET on Nasdaq, NYSE Arca, Cboe EDGX, MEMX and 24X. Premarket (4:00–9:30), regular hours (9:30–4:00) and after-hours (4:00–8:00) do not change, nor do the 9:30 open and 4:00 close auctions or the official close. Trades between 9 PM and midnight count toward the next trading day, the way futures work; overnight trades add to volume but do not set the day's last price, high or low; overnight is about 1% of share volume. No automatic trading pauses overnight: fixed 20% price bands, and a stock halted overnight stays halted until 4 AM. Clearing is unchanged: NSCC clears 24x5 and trades settle T+1 from the next-day trade date.
- [Covered Calls — get paid now, cap the upside](https://thetrademethod.com/covered-calls.html): Covered calls explained with real numbers: own 100 shares, sell a call against them and keep the premium. Four INTC outcomes, the break-even and the cap, the strike and duration trade-offs, and how to place the order.
- [Expected Move Calculator — the range the options market prices](https://thetrademethod.com/expected-move.html): An expected move dashboard: enter a ticker, expiration and the options chain prices (ATM straddle × 1.25, straddle plus first ITM strangle ÷ 2, implied volatility, or the 16 delta strikes) to get the upper and lower expected move drawn on a delayed price chart, compared with the stock's actual past moves and a weekly accuracy scorecard. Explains that the 68% is the odds of finishing inside at expiration (about 37% of staying inside all week), with SPY, QQQ and AAPL examples from June 3, 2022, and why a break outside the range is context, not a reversal signal.

## Famous strategies

- [Famous strategies](https://thetrademethod.com/famous-strategies/): famous, research-backed trading strategies for stocks and ETFs, one detailed animated page each (more pages being added).
- [Cross-Sectional Momentum — buy past winners, short past losers](https://thetrademethod.com/famous-strategies/cross-sectional-momentum.html): Jegadeesh and Titman's 1993 momentum strategy, animated: rank every stock on its last 3 to 12 months, buy the top tenth and short the bottom tenth, skip the latest stretch, hold 3 to 12 months in overlapping cohorts, what the paper found (1.31% a month for 12/3 in 1965–1989), why half of it fades, the 2009 momentum crash, and a free TradingView Pine Script indicator that ranks a list of stocks on 12-1 month momentum.
- [Post-Earnings Announcement Drift (PEAD), Explained](https://thetrademethod.com/famous-strategies/post-earnings-drift.html): Post-earnings announcement drift (Bernard and Thomas, 1989): after a big earnings surprise, stocks keep drifting the same way for weeks. How the surprise is scored, why the drift jumps at the next reports, how much it has faded, plus a free TradingView indicator.
- [Pairs Trading (Gatev, Goetzmann & Rouwenhorst), Explained](https://thetrademethod.com/famous-strategies/pairs-trading.html): Pairs trading (Gatev, Goetzmann and Rouwenhorst, 2006): match stocks whose prices moved together for a year, and when they split by two standard deviations, short the leader and buy the laggard until they cross. The rule, the paper's returns and costs, the risks, plus a free TradingView indicator.
- [Greenblatt's Magic Formula, Explained](https://thetrademethod.com/famous-strategies/magic-formula.html): Joel Greenblatt's Magic Formula: rank stocks on earnings yield and return on capital, add the ranks, and buy the best totals for a year. How the two numbers work, the book's 1988-2004 and updated results, why it loses some years, plus a free TradingView indicator.
- [Fama-French Value and Size Effects, Explained](https://thetrademethod.com/famous-strategies/value-and-size.html): The Fama-French value and size effects (1992, 1993): beta didn't explain returns, but size and book-to-market did. The sorts, the six boxes behind SMB and HML, how much the premiums shrank after publication, plus a free TradingView indicator.
- [The Low-Volatility Anomaly and Betting Against Beta, Explained](https://thetrademethod.com/famous-strategies/low-volatility.html): The low-volatility anomaly (Ang, Hodrick, Xing and Zhang, 2006; Frazzini and Pedersen, 2014): calm, low-beta stocks have earned about as much as wild ones, and far more per unit of risk. The flat beta line, the noisiest stocks' poor returns, betting against beta, why it lasts, plus a free TradingView indicator.
- [CAN SLIM (William O'Neil), Explained](https://thetrademethod.com/famous-strategies/can-slim.html): William O'Neil's CAN SLIM: seven letters for picking growth leaders (current and annual earnings, something new, supply and demand, leader, institutions, market), bought on breakouts from sound bases and sold at a 7-8% loss with no exceptions. The checklist, the cup with handle, the sell rules, the follow-through day, plus a free TradingView indicator.
- [Opening Range Breakout (ORB) on Stocks in Play, Explained](https://thetrademethod.com/famous-strategies/opening-range-breakout.html): The opening range breakout, from Toby Crabel (1990) to Zarattini, Barbon and Aziz (2024): the first 5-minute candle picks the side, a stop order at its high or low, a stop 10% of ATR away, out at the close, and only on stocks in play. 1,637% net in their 2016-2023 backtest against 29% without the filter. Animated walkthroughs plus a free TradingView indicator.
- [10-Month Moving Average Timing (Faber), Explained](https://thetrademethod.com/famous-strategies/ten-month-sma.html): Mebane Faber's 10-month moving average rule: once a month, hold an asset if it closed above its 10-month average, move to T-bills if it closed below. On the S&P 500 since 1901, about the same return as holding with far smaller drawdowns, and a five-asset version. Animated walkthroughs plus a free TradingView indicator.
- [Dual Momentum (Gary Antonacci, GEM), Explained](https://thetrademethod.com/famous-strategies/dual-momentum.html): Gary Antonacci's Dual Momentum and his Global Equities Momentum model: once a month, hold the stronger of US and non-US stocks over 12 months, but only if US stocks beat T-bills; otherwise hold bonds. 17.43% a year vs 8.85% for world stocks in his 1974-2013 backtest, with a 22.72% worst drawdown. Animated walkthroughs plus a free TradingView indicator.
- [Sector Rotation by Momentum (Faber, Moskowitz and Grinblatt), Explained](https://thetrademethod.com/famous-strategies/sector-rotation.html): Sector rotation by relative strength: rank ten sectors on trailing return each month and hold the top three. Moskowitz and Grinblatt (1999) found much of stock momentum is industry momentum; Faber (2010) found top sectors beat buy and hold by about 3-6% a year back to the 1920s. With a trend filter for bear markets. Animated walkthroughs plus a free TradingView indicator.
- [RSI(2) Pullback Strategy (Larry Connors), Explained](https://thetrademethod.com/famous-strategies/rsi-2.html): Larry Connors' RSI(2) strategy: buy an index ETF like SPY or QQQ above its 200-day average when the 2-period RSI drops to 5 or below, and sell on the first close above the 5-day average. Short, frequent trades with a high hit rate and no stop loss. Animated walkthroughs plus a free TradingView indicator.
- [Intraday Momentum: the First Half-Hour Predicts the Last](https://thetrademethod.com/famous-strategies/intraday-momentum.html): Gao, Han, Li and Zhou (2018): on SPY, the return from the previous close to 10:00 am predicts the direction of the last half-hour of the day. Long or short from 3:30 to 4:00 pm: 6.67% a year vs -1.11% for always long, 1993-2013, before costs, with an honest look at recent results. Animated walkthroughs plus a free TradingView indicator.
- [The Turn-of-the-Month Effect in Stocks, Explained](https://thetrademethod.com/famous-strategies/turn-of-the-month.html): The turn-of-the-month effect: US stock returns have clustered in four trading days, the last of each month and the first three of the next. McConnell and Xu (2008): 0.15% a day on those days vs -0.001% on the rest, 1926-2005, in 31 of 35 countries. How to trade it with an index fund, plus a free TradingView indicator.
- [The Overnight Effect: Why Stock Returns Come at Night](https://thetrademethod.com/famous-strategies/overnight-effect.html): The overnight effect: most of the US stock market's gain has come between the close and the next open, not during the trading day. Cliff, Cooper and Gulen (2008), 1993-2006: S&P 500 stocks averaged 0.028-0.048% a night and -0.028 to 0.002% a day. The numbers, the costs, and a free TradingView indicator.

## Test results

- [Tested results: do trading setups work?](https://thetrademethod.com/tested-results.html): our own backtests of 41 setups, fundamentals and famous strategies from this site, coded from each page's rules and run on five years of price data (Nov 2021 to Nov 2026) with costs and a random-entry benchmark. Only the Qullamaggie Breakout beat random entries (+0.63R a trade vs -0.21R); most setups broke even or lost after costs, and none of the 15 famous strategies beat holding SPY. Each tested page has a "We tested it" section with its numbers and caveats.

## Blog

- [Blog](https://thetrademethod.com/blog/): backtest results, trading research and notes, newest first.
- [Does the hitchhiker scalp work? (16,136 trades tested)](https://thetrademethod.com/blog/does-the-hitchhiker-scalp-work.html): Not on its own. The site's Hitchhiker Scalp indicator (SMB Capital's first pullback to the 9 EMA on the 2-minute chart after a strong move, stop on a 2-minute close past the 21 EMA, 70% trimmed into momentum and 30% trailed) was backtested at default settings on 10 large-cap US stocks (AAPL, AMD, COIN, GOOG, HOOD, META, MSFT, MU, NVDA, TSLA) plus SPY and QQQ from Nov 2021 to Nov 2026: 16,136 trades, 46% wins, profit factor 1.01, +0.006R per trade after 0.5 bp a side but -0.038R at 1 bp and -0.125R at 2 bp, 235R peak-to-low drawdown. Shorts +0.009R vs longs +0.003R; entries 9:30-10:30 +0.025R vs after 10:30 -0.011R; first hour plus 2.5x move volume +0.030R over 6,663 trades; the optional chop and daily mid-range skips added nothing; 6 of 12 symbols positive (COIN +0.08R best, QQQ -0.04R worst); the top 5% of trades made +2,735R. A TradingView AMD run with flat-at-close and first-hour-only filters made +1.8R on 33 trades. Cites Bailey et al. 2014 on backtest overfitting.
- [How does 23-hour stock trading work? (brokers, overnight volume and the new schedule)](https://thetrademethod.com/blog/how-23-hour-stock-trading-works.html): From Sunday, Dec 6, 2026, US stocks trade Sunday 9 PM to Friday 8 PM ET with an 8-9 PM pause each weeknight, so each trading day runs 23 hours (9 PM to 8 PM). Covers the hour-by-hour trading day, the 115-hour week, trade date and T+1 settlement for 9 PM-midnight trades, limit-only overnight orders (Nasdaq Night Session rejects unpriced orders), times in CT/PT/UTC, overnight halts (fixed 20% LULD price bands, no automatic pauses, a stock halted overnight stays halted until 4 AM; after a Level 3 market-wide halt Nasdaq waits until 4 AM), clearing (NSCC 24x5 since June 2026, T+1 from the next-day trade date), a table of brokers with overnight trading (Schwab thinkorswim, Interactive Brokers, Robinhood, Webull, moomoo, E*TRADE; Fidelity none) checked Nov 24, 2026, overnight volume (~1% of share volume, concentrated in large names), and starting liquidity rules (symbol, 50,000 shares traded, spread 0.10% or less, order 1% of volume or less, quarter to half size).
- [Do TradingView indicators beat random entries? (Introducing Backtest Board)](https://thetrademethod.com/blog/introducing-backtest-board.html): No. Backtest Board (backtestboard.com) tested 45 TradingView indicators on 28 markets (24 US stocks and ETFs, Bitcoin, XRP, Nasdaq-100 and S&P 500 futures) and 10 timeframes from 1 minute to 1 day, 23,608 backtests with real costs, no look-ahead, and training, validation and holdout periods. After costs, only 10 of 717 strategies were positive on validation and beat random entries with the same exit and filter on the holdout, about what luck alone would produce; none beat buy and hold (+73%) in the bull-market holdout. Includes the 10 shortlisted strategies, why random entries are the benchmark, the +10R cap, and an FAQ.
